newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana Land abandons Gulf subsalt well.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana Land abandons Gulf subsalt well.

text.p: Louisiana Land and Exploration Co said on Monday it successfully completed its LL&E Fee no. 1 well at West Paradis in south Louisiana, and it abandoned a subsalt well in the Gulf of Mexico.

In south Louisiana, Louisiana Land said the Fee no. 1 well flowed flowed 4 million cubic feet of natural gas and 74 barrels of condensate per day on a 14/64 inch choke with flowing tubing pressure of 3,853 pounds per square inch.
The well was drilled to a total measured depth of 12,567 feet and encountered 53 feet of net hydrocarbon pay in three zones, it said. Two remaining zones would be tested later, the company said.
Louisiana Land said its net revenue interest in the West Paradis prospect was 43 percent.
The company also said it abandoned a subsalt well on Ship Shoal Block 357 in the Gulf of Mexico.
The well was drilled to a total depth of 20,610 feet and no commercial hydrocarbon-bearing zones were encountered, it said. The well would be plugged and abandoned, it said.
Louisiana Land said it owned a 38 percent working interest in the well.
